messages:
Amy (Sales): Quick sync — NexusHealth POC is ready but legal redlined the MSA+DPA and procurement wants clarity on payment flow. They also flagged an odd signer path because the PO comes from a different org entity.
Matt (SE): Thanks — POC config: 3 GPUs, 8k context, token cap 50k/day. That materially affects the pricing line items we quoted.
Jordan (Legal): I looked at the redlines. Two blockers: 1) they changed our data retention SLA, 2) requested KMS attestation language. Can you share exact billing entity and whether customer insists on HSM-level wording?
Nina (Procurement): @Jordan they will pay from "NexusHealth, Inc." (US TAXID on the PO) but legal contact is in the EU subsidiary — so signature + invoicing mismatch. Procurement asks: do we need a PO on file to start the POC or can we accept a credit card for initial month?
Kevin (Finance): We can accept credit card for the hosted POC under a short-term invoice, but for enterprise billings we need a PO and Net30/Net45 preference. Which net terms did sales prospect mention?
Amy (Sales): Prospect verbally prefers Net45 for enterprise. For POC they'd prefer CC to avoid procurement delays. Also they asked if we can carve out logs from DPA for the POC period.
Matt (SE): Technically we can enable a temporary logs retention override for the POC (30 days) and tag it in the audit logs. That would avoid permanent DPA changes. Implementation note:
```
config.poc.retention_days = 30
audit.tag = "nexus-poc-temp"
```
Jordan (Legal): That sounds workable if the DPA appendix documents it as a time-limited exception and customer signs off. KMS/HSM: they asked for HSM attestation. We can provide our standard KMS integration statement but not HSM attestation unless we have a dedicated addendum.
Nina (Procurement): Ok — procurement will accept CC for initial month if finance confirms no revenue recognition issues and legal gets a signed appendix for the retention exception. Also need a contact for invoice recipient (name/email) — send that and we'll route.
Kevin (Finance): No revrec issues for <30 day CC trial. If they convert to committed Dedicated later, we'll need PO and billing address. Also confirm tax handling (US vs EU VAT).
Amy (Sales): I'll confirm billing contact and tax entity tonight. Quick question on signatures: they prefer an internal e-sign tool that routes to multiple signers in sequence (legal -> finance -> exec). Does DocuSign chain work or do we need to handle any special fields for multi-entity signing?
Jordan (Legal): DocuSign standard ordering works. If the PO is from a different entity, we need the order form to show both: invoicing entity and signing entity. Legal prefers an explicit signature block per legal entity.
Matt (SE): One more: pricing for POC as quoted included burst credits — confirm if procurement wants those removed (lower cost) during trial. If removed, we'll update order form lines.
Amy (Sales): Procurement asked to remove burst credits to keep trial cost predictable. We'll take that change.
Jordan (Legal): Action: I'll draft a short POC appendix (retention exception + signature blocks + KMS statement) and circulate.
Nina (Procurement): Action: Send invoice recipient info to nina.procurement@nexushc.com and attach the PO if they have one. We'll route for countersign.
Kevin (Finance): Action: Finance approves CC for month-1. I'll standby for final billing entity and VAT details.
Amy (Sales): I'll update order form (remove burst credits) and attach updated lines. Expect draft appendix from Jordan by EOD. Thanks :thumbsup:
